session_uid.description: The native session identifier reported by the CLI (ACP session). Not a Journal run identifier.

record_type.caption: Record Type
record_type.description: The native record discriminator (for example type/subtype or event name) as the mapping contract defines it.

parse_status_id.caption: Parse Status ID
parse_status_id.description: Whether the retained record could be parsed as one JSON object.

2.caption: Malformed JSON
2.description: Decodable text that is not one JSON object (including duplicate keys under strict parsing).

3.caption: Undecodable bytes
3.description: The line is not valid UTF-8; raw_bytes_b64 holds the bytes.

4.caption: Blank
4.description: An empty line, retained to preserve framing.

5.caption: Incomplete at source end
5.description: The source ended (EOF or interruption) without a line terminator while the record was not yet one JSON object; the bytes received are retained verbatim.

basis.caption: Basis
basis.description: Why the record was retained whole (no rule, or the parse failure reason).

data.caption: Data
data.description: The parsed record exactly as reported.

raw_bytes_b64.caption: Raw Bytes (base64)
raw_bytes_b64.description: The exact bytes of a record that cannot be represented as a JSON string.

end_time_dt.caption: End Time
end_time_dt.description: The time of the most recent event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

start_time_dt.caption: Start Time
start_time_dt.description: The time of the earliest event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

time_dt.caption: Event Time
time_dt.description: The primary timestamp of the event - when the activity actually occurred at the source. This does not capture when the event record was created or serialized by the source system; for event lifecycle timestamps such as ingestion and processing, use metadata.logged_time and metadata.processed_time respectively, or the equivalent attributes in the metadata.loggers array when recording pipeline stages. For aggregate events (count > 1), set this to start_time (the earliest OCSF time in the aggregate) to preserve causal ordering and consistent timeline alignment. Note: finding classes redefine time as the finding creation time rather than the activity occurrence time. This must be a UTC epoch value in milliseconds (e.g., 1776881335332). Mappers should use the most precise and authoritative timestamp available from the source.

agentic_cli/tool_call.caption: Tool Call
agentic_cli/tool_call.description: An ACP tool call lifecycle observation: the request, an observed result, or a separately reported operation within the call. Request state, permission decision, execution state and result stay distinct attributes.
agentic_cli/tool_call.name: tool_call

action_id.caption: Action ID
action_id.description: The action taken by a control or other policy-based system leading to an outcome or disposition. An unknown action may still correspond to a known disposition. Refer to disposition_id for the outcome of the action.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The action was unknown. The disposition_id attribute may still be set to a non-unknown value, for example 'Custom Action', 'Challenge'.

1.caption: Allowed
1.description: The activity was allowed. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Allowed', 'Approved', 'Delayed', 'No Action', 'Count' etc.

2.caption: Denied
2.description: The attempted activity was denied. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Blocked', 'Rejected', 'Quarantined', 'Isolated', 'Dropped', 'Access Revoked, etc.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The action is not mapped. See the action attribute which contains a data source specific value.

3.caption: Observed
3.description: The activity was observed, but neither explicitly allowed nor denied. This is common with IDS and EDR controls that report additional information on observed behavior such as TTPs. The disposition_id attribute should be set to a value that conforms to this action, for example 'Logged', 'Alert', 'Detected', 'Count', etc.

4.caption: Modified
4.description: The activity was modified, adjusted, or corrected. The disposition_id attribute should be set appropriately, for example 'Restored', 'Corrected', 'Delayed', 'Captcha', 'Tagged'.

attacks.caption: MITRE ATT&CK® and ATLAS™ Details
attacks.description: An array of MITRE ATT&CK® objects describing identified tactics, techniques & sub-techniques. The objects are compatible with MITRE ATLAS™ tactics, techniques & sub-techniques.

authorizations.caption: Authorization Information
authorizations.description: Provides details about an authorization, such as authorization outcome, and any associated policies related to the activity/event.

confidence.caption: Confidence
confidence.description: The confidence, normalized to the caption of the confidence_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

confidence_id.caption: Confidence ID
confidence_id.description: The normalized confidence refers to the accuracy of the security control or alert. An analytic with a low confidence means that the alerts may be noisy or may not be malicious in nature.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The confidence is not mapped to the defined enum values. See the confidence attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

confidence_score.caption: Confidence Score
confidence_score.description: The confidence score as reported by the event source. If confidence_id is 99 'Other', it should be the same as confidence if both are populated.

disposition.caption: Disposition
disposition.description: The disposition name, normalized to the caption of the disposition_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

disposition_id.caption: Disposition ID
disposition_id.description: Describes the outcome or action taken by a security control, such as access control checks, malware detections or various types of policy violations.

1.caption: Allowed
1.description: Granted access or allowed the action to the protected resource.

2.caption: Blocked
2.description: Denied access or blocked the action to the protected resource.

3.caption: Quarantined
3.description: A suspicious file or other content was moved to a benign location.

4.caption: Isolated
4.description: A session was isolated on the network or within a browser.

5.caption: Deleted
5.description: A file or other content was deleted.

6.caption: Dropped
6.description: The request was detected as a threat and resulted in the connection being dropped.

7.caption: Custom Action
7.description: A custom action was executed such as running of a command script. Use the message attribute of the base class for details.

8.caption: Approved
8.description: A request or submission was approved. For example, when a form was properly filled out and submitted. This is distinct from 1 'Allowed'.

9.caption: Restored
9.description: A quarantined file or other content was restored to its original location.

10.caption: Exonerated
10.description: A suspicious or risky entity was deemed to no longer be suspicious (re-scored).

11.caption: Corrected
11.description: A corrupt file or configuration was corrected.

12.caption: Partially Corrected
12.description: A corrupt file or configuration was partially corrected.

13.caption: Uncorrected
13.description: A corrupt file or configuration was not corrected.

14.caption: Delayed
14.description: An operation was delayed, for example if a restart was required to finish the operation.

15.caption: Detected
15.description: Suspicious activity or a policy violation was detected without further action.

16.caption: No Action
16.description: The outcome of an operation had no action taken.

17.caption: Logged
17.description: The operation or action was logged without further action.

18.caption: Tagged
18.description: A file or other entity was marked with extended attributes.

19.caption: Alert
19.description: The request or activity was detected as a threat and resulted in a notification but request was not blocked.

20.caption: Count
20.description: Counted the request or activity but did not determine whether to allow it or block it.

21.caption: Reset
21.description: The request was detected as a threat and resulted in the connection being reset.

22.caption: Captcha
22.description: Required the end user to solve a CAPTCHA puzzle to prove that a human being is sending the request.

23.caption: Challenge
23.description: Ran a silent challenge that required the client session to verify that it's a browser, and not a bot.

24.caption: Access Revoked
24.description: The requestor's access has been revoked due to security policy enforcements. Note: use the Host profile if the User or Actor requestor is not present in the event class.

25.caption: Rejected
25.description: A request or submission was rejected. For example, when a form was improperly filled out and submitted. This is distinct from 2 'Blocked'.

26.caption: Unauthorized
26.description: An attempt to access a resource was denied due to an authorization check that failed. This is a more specific disposition than 2 'Blocked' and can be complemented with the authorizations attribute for more detail.

27.caption: Error
27.description: An error occurred during the processing of the activity or request. Use the message attribute of the base class for details.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The disposition is not mapped. See the disposition attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

firewall_rule.caption: Firewall Rule
firewall_rule.description: The firewall rule that pertains to the control that triggered the event, if applicable.

is_alert.caption: Alert
is_alert.description: Indicates that the event is considered to be an alertable signal. Should be set to true if disposition_id = Alert among other dispositions, and/or risk_level_id or severity_id of the event is elevated. Not all control events will be alertable, for example if disposition_id = Exonerated or disposition_id = Allowed.

malware.caption: Malware
malware.description: A list of Malware objects, describing details about the identified malware.

malware_scan_info.caption: Malware Scan Info
malware_scan_info.description: Describes details about the scan job that identified malware on the target system.

policy.caption: Policy
policy.description: The policy that pertains to the control that triggered the event, if applicable. For example the name of an anti-malware policy or an access control policy.

risk_details.caption: Risk Details
risk_details.description: Describes the risk associated with the finding.

risk_level.caption: Risk Level
risk_level.description: The risk level, normalized to the caption of the risk_level_id value.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The risk level is not mapped. See the risk_level attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

risk_score.caption: Risk Score
risk_score.description: The risk score as reported by the event source.

attestation_list.caption: Attestation List
attestation_list.description: One or more cryptographic attestation objects over an event, each providing integrity, authenticity, and non-repudiation. Independent attesters over the same event — for example a producer at write time and a downstream processor at ingest — each contribute a separate attestation, distinct from co-signers on a single attestation, which share its signatures array. Carried on the record_integrity profile; the object itself is domain-agnostic.

osint.caption: OSINT
osint.description: The OSINT (Open Source Intelligence) object contains details related to an indicator such as the indicator itself, related indicators, geolocation, registrar information, subdomains, analyst commentary, and other contextual information. This information can be used to further enrich a detection or finding by providing decisioning support to other analysts and engineers.

actor.caption: Actor
actor.description: The user, process, or service that initiated the activity on the host. For system-level events this is typically a process; for IAM events it is typically a user or role.

device.caption: Device
device.description: The host or device where the activity was observed. Populate with details such as hostname, IP address, OS, and hardware identifiers when available from the source.

api.caption: API Details
api.description: Describes details about a typical API (Application Programming Interface) call.

cloud.caption: Cloud
cloud.description: Describes details about the Cloud environment where the event or finding was created.

activity_id.caption: Activity ID
activity_id.description: The normalized identifier of the activity that triggered the event. Each event class defines its own set of activity values. Use 0 (Unknown) when the activity cannot be determined. Use 99 (Other) when the activity does not match any defined value, in which case activity_name must be populated with the source-specific label.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The event activity is not mapped. See the activity_name attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

1.caption: Requested
1.description: A tool request was observed.

2.caption: Result observed
2.description: A result for a tool request was observed.

3.caption: Operation observed
3.description: A separately reported operation of a tool call was observed.

activity_name.caption: Activity
activity_name.description: The event activity name, as defined by the activity_id. When activity_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific activity label. For all other activity_id values, this must match the caption defined for that activity_id enum value.

category_name.caption: Category
category_name.description: The event category name, as defined by category_uid value: Agent Execution.

category_uid.caption: Category ID
category_uid.description: The category unique identifier of the event. Each event class belongs to exactly one category. Producers and mappers must set this to the category defined by the event class being used.

90111.caption: Agent Execution
90111.description: Observed execution of an agentic CLI: prompt turns, model responses, tool calls and their operations, and retained native source records.

class_name.caption: Class
class_name.description: The event class name, as defined by class_uid value: Tool Call.

class_uid.caption: Class ID
class_uid.description: The unique identifier of a class. A class describes the attributes available in an event. Producers and mappers must set this to the uid defined in the event class definition. For example, Detection Finding is 2004.

90111003.caption: Tool Call
90111003.description: An ACP tool call lifecycle observation: the request, an observed result, or a separately reported operation within the call. Request state, permission decision, execution state and result stay distinct attributes.

count.caption: Count
count.description: The number of events aggregated into this single record. Only populate for aggregate events. When set, start_time and end_time should also be provided to define the aggregation window.

duration.caption: Duration Milliseconds
duration.description: The elapsed time of the aggregation window in milliseconds, from start_time to end_time. Only populate for aggregate events (count > 1). The value should equal end_time - start_time.

end_time.caption: End Time
end_time.description: The time of the most recent event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

enrichments.caption: Enrichments
enrichments.description:
The additional information from an external data source, which is associated with the event or a finding. For example add location information for the IP address in the DNS answers:

[{"name": "answers.ip", "value": "92.24.47.250", "type": "location", "data": {"city": "Socotra", "continent": "Asia", "coordinates": [-25.4153, 17.0743], "country": "YE", "desc": "Yemen"}}]

message.caption: Message
message.description: A human-readable description of the event, as defined by the source. This should be a concise, meaningful summary suitable for display in a UI or alert notification - not a raw log line. For example: "User john_doe logged in from 10.0.0.1." rather than a raw syslog string.

metadata.caption: Metadata
metadata.description: The metadata object describes the event producer, schema version, and processing information. Producers and mappers must populate metadata.product to identify the data source, and metadata.version to indicate the OCSF schema version used. Consumers rely on this to interpret the event correctly.

observables.caption: Observables
observables.description: The observables array surfaces key indicators and entities from the event or finding in a single, consistent location for downstream correlation and detection. Each entry references an attribute path within the event (e.g., src_endpoint.ip) along with its type and value, enabling consumers to extract IOCs without parsing the full event structure.

raw_data.caption: Raw Data
raw_data.description: The original event/finding data as received from the source, before normalization into OCSF. Populate this with the verbatim log line, JSON payload, or other native format for forensic and debugging purposes. This field is not intended for structured querying - use the normalized OCSF attributes instead.

raw_data_hash.caption: Raw Data Hash
raw_data_hash.description: A fingerprint (hash) of the raw_data content. Use this to verify the integrity of the original event data or to deduplicate events.

raw_data_size.caption: Raw Data Size
raw_data_size.description: The size of the original event data (as captured in raw_data) in bytes, before OCSF normalization. Useful for metering and capacity planning.

severity.caption: Severity
severity.description: The event/finding severity label, normalized to the caption of the severity_id value. When severity_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific severity label. For all other values, this should match the caption defined for that severity_id enum value (e.g., "High" for severity_id: 4).

severity_id.caption: Severity ID
severity_id.description:
The normalized identifier of the event/finding severity.

The normalized severity is a measurement the effort and expense required to manage and resolve an event or incident. Smaller numerical values represent lower impact events, and larger numerical values represent higher impact events.

1.caption: Informational
1.description: Informational message. No action required.

2.caption: Low
2.description: The user decides if action is needed.

3.caption: Medium
3.description: Action is required but the situation is not serious at this time.

4.caption: High
4.description: Action is required immediately.

5.caption: Critical
5.description: Action is required immediately and the scope is broad.

6.caption: Fatal
6.description: An error occurred but it is too late to take remedial action.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The event/finding severity is not mapped. See the severity attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

start_time.caption: Start Time
start_time.description: The time of the earliest event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

status.caption: Status
status.description: The event status label, normalized to the caption of the status_id value. When status_id is 99 (Other), this attribute must contain the source-specific status label. For all other values, this must match the caption defined for that status_id enum value (e.g., "Success" for status_id: 1).

status_code.caption: Status Code
status_code.description: The source-specific status or error code as reported by the event source. For example, a Windows logon failure code (0x18), an HTTP response code (403), or an AWS API error code. This preserves the original code for detailed troubleshooting beyond what status_id conveys.

status_detail.caption: Status Detail
status_detail.description: A human-readable description providing additional context about the event outcome. Use this to convey details that go beyond the normalized status_id and source-specific status_code, such as a failure reason or error message. For example: "Account locked after 5 failed attempts.".

status_id.caption: Status ID
status_id.description: The normalized status of the event outcome. Use this family of attributes to convey the outcome of the activity described by the event. Producers should map their source outcome to 1 (Success) or 2 (Failure). Use 0 (Unknown) when the outcome cannot be determined, and 99 (Other) with a populated status string when the source value does not map cleanly.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The status is not mapped. See the status attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

1.caption: Success
1.description: The activity completed successfully.

2.caption: Failure
2.description: The activity failed.

time.caption: Event Time
time.description: The primary timestamp of the event - when the activity actually occurred at the source. This does not capture when the event record was created or serialized by the source system; for event lifecycle timestamps such as ingestion and processing, use metadata.logged_time and metadata.processed_time respectively, or the equivalent attributes in the metadata.loggers array when recording pipeline stages. For aggregate events (count > 1), set this to start_time (the earliest OCSF time in the aggregate) to preserve causal ordering and consistent timeline alignment. Note: finding classes redefine time as the finding creation time rather than the activity occurrence time. This must be a UTC epoch value in milliseconds (e.g., 1776881335332). Mappers should use the most precise and authoritative timestamp available from the source.

timezone_offset.caption: Timezone Offset
timezone_offset.description: The number of minutes that the reported event time is ahead or behind UTC, in the range -1,080 to +1,080. This allows consumers to reconstruct the local time at the event source. For example, US Eastern Standard Time is -300. Populate this when the source provides local time zone information.

type_name.caption: Type Name
type_name.description: The event/finding type name, combining the class and activity (e.g., "Detection Finding: Create"). The value must match the class_name and activity_name joined by ": ".

type_uid.caption: Type ID
type_uid.description: The event/finding type ID. It identifies the event's semantics and structure. Producers and mappers must compute this as class_uid * 100 + activity_id. It uniquely identifies the combination of event class and activity across the entire schema. For example, Detection Finding: Create is 200401.

9011100302.caption: Tool Call: Result observed
9011100302.description: A result for a tool request was observed.

9011100303.caption: Tool Call: Operation observed
9011100303.description: A separately reported operation of a tool call was observed.

unmapped.caption: Unmapped Data
unmapped.description:
A container for source-specific attributes that do not map to any defined OCSF attribute. Use this to preserve valuable source data that would otherwise be lost during normalization. The keys and values are specific to the event source.

Note: Consumers should not rely on a stable structure within this field. The preferred approach to unmapped attributes is to create a custom extension with the desired structure.

references.description: Schema FAQ: When should I use the unmapped attribute?

cli_agent.caption: CLI Agent
cli_agent.description: The CLI agent is stored once per run in run.json shared.cli_agent (0.2.0); it is present on an event only in a self-contained export.

journal.caption: Journal Provenance
journal.description: Agent Journal's own provenance for this event: run and invocation identity, producer, mapping contract, capture time and sequence. Distinct from metadata.product, which names the originating CLI.

source_ref.caption: Source Reference
source_ref.description: Which native source artifact and record occurrence supplied the facts in this event or object.

session_uid.caption: Session ID
session_uid.description: The native session identifier reported by the CLI (ACP session). Not a Journal run identifier.

turn_uid.caption: Prompt Turn ID
turn_uid.description: The native identifier of the prompt turn, when the source reports one.

response_uid.caption: Model Response ID
response_uid.description: The native identifier of the model response (for example the Anthropic message id).

tool_call_uid.caption: Tool Call ID
tool_call_uid.description: The native identifier of the tool call request. Absent when the source does not report one for the record.

identity_basis_id.caption: Identity Basis ID
identity_basis_id.description: What kind of identifier tool_call_uid is, when a declared rule states it.

1.caption: Model-facing call identifier
1.description: The identifier the model's own tool request carried, as the source reports it.

2.caption: Stream-local item identifier
2.description: An identifier the CLI's output stream assigns to its own items; unique within that stream only; the model-facing call identifier is not reported.

tool_name.caption: Tool Name
tool_name.description: The exact tool name as reported by the CLI. Never normalized.

tool_namespace.caption: Tool Namespace
tool_namespace.description: The namespace the source reports beside the tool name, such as the MCP server of an MCP tool. Absent when the source reports none; never derived from the tool name.

tool_kind_id.caption: Tool Kind ID
tool_kind_id.description: The ACP tool kind of the requested tool activity, assigned by a declared mapping rule named in tool_kind_basis. A kind describes the request; it is not evidence of an operating-system effect.

tool_kind.caption: Tool Kind
tool_kind.description: The ACP tool kind caption, sibling of tool_kind_id.

tool_kind_basis.caption: Tool Kind Basis
tool_kind_basis.description: The mapping rule that assigned tool_kind_id (for example a name-to-kind table id). Shell command parsing is not a permitted basis.

arguments.caption: Tool Arguments
arguments.description: The tool request arguments exactly as the source reported them (object, string or other JSON value).

tool_result.caption: Tool Result
tool_result.description: The observed result of a tool call as the source returned it.

tool_operation.caption: Operation
tool_operation.description: A separately reported operation executed within a tool call (for example one command of a multi-command exec).

reported_state.caption: Reported State
reported_state.description: The request/result lifecycle state string exactly as the source reported it (for example ACTIVE, DONE, completed).

permission_decision.caption: Permission Decision
permission_decision.description: A permission decision reported by the source at its reported scope.

status_basis_id.caption: Status Basis ID
status_basis_id.description: Whether status_id was reported by the source, derived by a declared Journal rule, or could not be derived.

derivation.caption: Derivation
derivation.description: Identifier of the declared rule and inputs used to derive a value.

data.caption: Data
data.description: Native record fields not represented elsewhere on the event (residual).

end_time_dt.caption: End Time
end_time_dt.description: The time of the most recent event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

start_time_dt.caption: Start Time
start_time_dt.description: The time of the earliest event in an aggregate (count > 1). Do not populate for discrete, point-in-time events - use time alone. Subclasses such as findings may redefine this for their own time-range semantics.

time_dt.caption: Event Time
time_dt.description: The primary timestamp of the event - when the activity actually occurred at the source. This does not capture when the event record was created or serialized by the source system; for event lifecycle timestamps such as ingestion and processing, use metadata.logged_time and metadata.processed_time respectively, or the equivalent attributes in the metadata.loggers array when recording pipeline stages. For aggregate events (count > 1), set this to start_time (the earliest OCSF time in the aggregate) to preserve causal ordering and consistent timeline alignment. Note: finding classes redefine time as the finding creation time rather than the activity occurrence time. This must be a UTC epoch value in milliseconds (e.g., 1776881335332). Mappers should use the most precise and authoritative timestamp available from the source.

account.caption: Account
account.description: The Account object contains details about the account that initiated or performed a specific activity within a system or application. Additionally, the Account object refers to logical Cloud and Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) based containers such as AWS Accounts, Azure Subscriptions, Oracle Cloud Compartments, Google Cloud Projects, and otherwise.
account.name: account

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the account (e.g. GCP Project name , Linux Account name or AWS Account name).

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the account (e.g. AWS Account ID , OCID , GCP Project ID , Azure Subscription ID , Google Workspace Customer ID , or M365 Tenant UID).

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

is_disabled.caption: Disabled
is_disabled.description: Indicates if the account is disabled.

is_locked.caption: Locked
is_locked.description: Indicates if the account is locked. For example, due to the amount of failed logins.

is_on_premises_sync_enabled.caption: On-Premises Sync Enabled
is_on_premises_sync_enabled.description: Indicates whether synchronization with an on-premises directory service is enabled. For example, Microsoft Entra Connect.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The list of labels associated to the account.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the account.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The account type, normalized to the caption of 'account_type_id'. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The account type is not mapped.

6.caption: Azure AD Account
6.description: Note: The new product name for Azure AD is Microsoft Entra ID.

actor.caption: Actor
actor.description: The Actor object contains details about the user, role, application, service, or process that initiated or performed a specific activity. Note that Actor is not the threat actor of a campaign but may be part of a campaign. When the initiator of the activity is an autonomous AI agent, apply the ai_operation profile and populate ai_operation.ai_agent rather than describing the agent here.
actor.name: actor

app_name.caption: Application Name
app_name.description: The client application or service that initiated the activity. This can be in conjunction with the user if present. Note that app_name is distinct from the process if present.

app_uid.caption: Application ID
app_uid.description: The unique identifier of the client application or service that initiated the activity. This can be in conjunction with the user if present. Note that app_name is distinct from the process.pid or process.uid if present.

application.caption: Application
application.description: The client application or service that initiated the activity. This can be in conjunction with the user if present. Note that application is distinct from the process if present.

authorizations.caption: Authorization Information
authorizations.description: Provides details about an authorization, such as authorization outcome, and any associated policies related to the activity/event.

iam_role.caption: IAM Role
iam_role.description: The actor's role, or as an alternative to user or process when the role is serving as a security principal for the operation that initiated the activity.

idp.caption: Identity Provider
idp.description: This object describes details about the Identity Provider used.

invoked_by.caption: Invoked by
invoked_by.description: The name of the service that invoked the activity as described in the event.

process.caption: Process
process.description: The process that initiated the activity.

session.caption: Session
session.description: The user session from which the activity was initiated.

user.caption: User
user.description: The user that initiated the activity or the user context from which the activity was initiated.

advisory.caption: Advisory
advisory.description: The Advisory object represents publicly disclosed cybersecurity vulnerabilities defined in a Security advisory. e.g. Microsoft KB Article, Apple Security Advisory, or a GitHub Security Advisory (GHSA)
advisory.name: advisory

classification.caption: Classification
classification.description: The vendors classification of the Advisory.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The time when the Advisory record was created.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: A brief description of the Advisory Record.

install_state.caption: Install State
install_state.description: The install state of the Advisory.

install_state_id.caption: Install State ID
install_state_id.description: The normalized install state ID of the Advisory.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The normalized install state is unknown.

1.caption: Installed
1.description: The item is installed.

2.caption: Not Installed
2.description: The item is not installed.

3.caption: Installed Pending Reboot
3.description: The item is installed pending reboot operation.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The install state is not mapped. See the install_state attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

is_superseded.caption: The patch is superseded.
is_superseded.description: The Advisory has been replaced by another.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The time when the Advisory record was last updated.

os.caption: OS
os.description: The operating system the Advisory applies to.

product.caption: Product
product.description: The product where the vulnerability was discovered.

references.caption: References
references.description: A list of reference URLs with additional information about the vulnerabilities disclosed in the Advisory.

related_cves.caption: Related CVEs
related_cves.description: A list of Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) identifiers related to the vulnerabilities disclosed in the Advisory.

related_cwes.caption: Related CWEs
related_cwes.description: A list of Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) identifiers related to the vulnerabilities disclosed in the Advisory.

size.caption: Size
size.description: The size in bytes for the Advisory. Usually populated for a KB Article patch.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The Advisory link from the source vendor.

title.caption: Title
title.description: A title or a brief phrase summarizing the Advisory.

uid.caption: Advisory ID
uid.description: The unique identifier assigned to the advisory or disclosed vulnerability, e.g, GHSA-5mrr-rgp6-x4gr.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time
created_time_dt.description: The time when the Advisory record was created.

modified_time_dt.caption: Modified Time
modified_time_dt.description: The time when the Advisory record was last updated.

affected_code.caption: Affected Code
affected_code.description: The Affected Code object describes details about a code block identified as vulnerable.
affected_code.name: affected_code

end_column.caption: End Column
end_column.description: The column number of the last part of the assessed code identified as vulnerable.

end_line.caption: End Line
end_line.description: The line number of the last line of code block identified as vulnerable.

file.caption: File
file.description: Details about the file that contains the affected code block.

owner.caption: Owner
owner.description: Details about the user that owns the affected file.

remediation.caption: Remediation Guidance
remediation.description: Describes the recommended remediation steps to address identified issue(s).

rule.caption: Related Rule
rule.description: Details about the specific rule, e.g., those defined as part of a larger policy, that triggered the finding.

start_column.caption: Start Column
start_column.description: The column number of the first part of the assessed code identified as vulnerable.

start_line.caption: Start Line
start_line.description: The line number of the first line of code block identified as vulnerable.

affected_package.caption: Affected Software Package
affected_package.description: The Affected Package object describes details about a software package identified as affected by a vulnerability/vulnerabilities.
affected_package.name: affected_package

architecture.caption: Architecture
architecture.description: Architecture is a shorthand name describing the type of computer hardware the packaged software is meant to run on.

cpe_name.caption: The product CPE identifier
cpe_name.description: The Common Platform Enumeration (CPE) name. For example: cpe:/a:apple:safari:16.2.

epoch.caption: Epoch
epoch.description: The software package epoch. Epoch is a way to define weighted dependencies based on version numbers.

hash.caption: Hash
hash.description: Cryptographic hash to identify the binary instance of a software component. This can include any component such file, package, or library.

license.caption: Software License
license.description: The software license applied to this package.

license_url.caption: Software License URL
license_url.description: The URL pointing to the license applied on package or software. This is typically a LICENSE.md file within a repository.

name.caption: Name
name.description: The software package name.

package_manager.caption: Package Manager
package_manager.description: The software packager manager utilized to manage a package on a system, e.g. npm, yum, dpkg etc.

package_manager_url.caption: Package Manager URL
package_manager_url.description: The URL of the package or library at the package manager, or the specific URL or URI of an internal package manager link such as AWS CodeArtifact or Artifactory.

purl.caption: Package URL
purl.description: A purl is a URL string used to identify and locate a software package in a mostly universal and uniform way across programming languages, package managers, packaging conventions, tools, APIs and databases.

release.caption: Software Release Details
release.description: Release is the number of times a version of the software has been packaged.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The link to the specific library or package such as within GitHub, this is different from the link to the package manager where the library or package is hosted.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of software package, normalized to the caption of the type_id value. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the source.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

1.caption: Application
1.description: An application software package.

2.caption: Operating System
2.description: An operating system software package.

uid.caption: Package UID
uid.description: A unique identifier for the package or library reported by the source tool. E.g., the libId within the sbom field of an OX Security Issue or the SPDX components.*.bom-ref.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The name of the vendor who published the software package.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The software package version.

fixed_in_version.caption: Fixed In Version
fixed_in_version.description: The software package version in which a reported vulnerability was patched/fixed.

path.caption: Path
path.description: The installation path of the affected package.

remediation.caption: Remediation Guidance
remediation.description: Describes the recommended remediation steps to address identified issue(s).

agent.caption: Agent
agent.description: An Agent (also known as a Sensor) is typically installed on an Operating System (OS) and serves as a specialized software component that can be designed to monitor, detect, collect, archive, or take action. These activities and possible actions are defined by the upstream system controlling the Agent and its intended purpose. For instance, an Agent can include Endpoint Detection & Response (EDR) agents, backup/disaster recovery sensors, Application Performance Monitoring or profiling sensors, and similar software.
agent.name: agent

name.caption: Agent Name
name.description: The name of the agent or sensor. For example: AWS SSM Agent.

policies.caption: Agent Policies
policies.description: Describes the various policies that may be applied or enforced by an agent or sensor. E.g., Conditional Access, prevention, auto-update, tamper protection, destination configuration, etc.

type.caption: Agent Type
type.description: The normalized caption of the type_id value for the agent or sensor. In the case of 'Other' or 'Unknown', it is defined by the event source.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The normalized representation of an agent or sensor. E.g., EDR, vulnerability management, APM, backup & recovery, etc.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The type is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

1.caption: Endpoint Detection and Response
1.description: Any EDR sensor or agent. Or any tool that provides similar threat detection, anti-malware, anti-ransomware, or similar capabilities. E.g., Crowdstrike Falcon, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, Wazuh.

2.caption: Data Loss Prevention
2.description: Any DLP sensor or agent. Or any tool that provides similar data classification, data loss detection, and/or data loss prevention capabilities. E.g., Forcepoint DLP, Microsoft Purview, Symantec DLP.

3.caption: Backup & Recovery
3.description: Any agent or sensor that provides backups, archival, or recovery capabilities. E.g., Azure Backup, AWS Backint Agent.

4.caption: Performance Monitoring & Observability
4.description: Any agent or sensor that provides Application Performance Monitoring (APM), active tracing, profiling, or other observability use cases and optionally forwards the logs. E.g., New Relic Agent, Datadog Agent, Azure Monitor Agent.

5.caption: Vulnerability Management
5.description: Any agent or sensor that provides vulnerability management or scanning capabilities. E.g., Qualys VMDR, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, Crowdstrike Spotlight, Amazon Inspector Agent.

6.caption: Log Forwarding
6.description: Any agent or sensor that forwards logs to a 3rd party storage system such as a data lake or SIEM. E.g., Splunk Universal Forwarder, Tenzir, FluentBit, Amazon CloudWatch Agent, Amazon Kinesis Agent.

7.caption: Mobile Device Management
7.description: Any agent or sensor responsible for providing Mobile Device Management (MDM) or Mobile Enterprise Management (MEM) capabilities. E.g., JumpCloud Agent, Esper Agent, Jamf Pro binary.

8.caption: Configuration Management
8.description: Any agent or sensor that provides configuration management of a device, such as scanning for software, license management, or applying configurations. E.g., AWS Systems Manager Agent, Flexera, ServiceNow MID Server.

9.caption: Remote Access
9.description: Any agent or sensor that provides remote access capabilities to a device. E.g., BeyondTrust, Amazon Systems Manager Agent, Verkada Agent.

uid.caption: Agent ID
uid.description: The UID of the agent or sensor, sometimes known as a Sensor ID or aid.

uid_alt.caption: Alternate Agent ID
uid_alt.description: An alternative or contextual identifier for the agent or sensor, such as a configuration, organization, or license UID.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The company or author who created the agent or sensor. For example: Crowdstrike.

version.caption: Agent Version
version.description: The semantic version of the agent or sensor, e.g., 7.101.50.0.

agentic_cli/attribution.caption: Attribution
agentic_cli/attribution.description: The declared outcome of associating a fact with an owner, and how the candidates were obtained (reported identifier or derived by rule).
agentic_cli/attribution.name: attribution

outcome_id.caption: Attribution Outcome ID
outcome_id.description: Whether the owner of a fact could be established from the source.

1.caption: Unique
1.description: Exactly one owner is established by the declared join keys.

2.caption: Ambiguous
2.description: More than one candidate owner satisfies the declared join keys; the fact is attached at the enclosing scope only.

3.caption: Unattributed
3.description: The source provides no key to any owner; the fact is retained at its reported scope.

candidates.caption: Candidate Owners
candidates.description: Identifiers of the candidate owners considered.

basis.caption: Basis
basis.description: The declared rule, join keys or reason behind a classification, derivation or fallback.

scope_uid.caption: Scope ID
scope_uid.description: Identifier of the scope within which candidates were considered (for example a turn id).

method_id.caption: Attribution Method ID
method_id.description: How the candidate owners of an attribution were obtained: from an identifier the source record itself reports at the declared path, or by a declared derivation rule (for example text containment within a scope). A derived association is never a reported parent identifier.

1.caption: Reported identifier
1.description: The source record names the owner at the declared path.

2.caption: Derived by rule
2.description: Candidates were computed by the declared rule named in basis; the source reports no owner identifier.

agentic_cli/cli_agent.caption: CLI Agent
agentic_cli/cli_agent.description: An agentic CLI observed by Agent Journal, defined by this extension (since 0.4.0-prototype it does not extend the core ai_agent, whose framework-agent vocabulary does not describe an agentic CLI). product identifies the CLI product and version; name is the product name; version is the CLI version; instance_uid is the native session id; uid is set only when a source reports a stable logical agent identity. Launch settings and source references belong to the run manifest and source_ref, not to this object.
agentic_cli/cli_agent.name: cli_agent

name.caption: Name
name.description: The CLI product name.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The CLI version, as the source reports it or as the adapter's documented discovery found it.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: A stable logical agent identity, set only when a source reports one; never the product name or a session id.

instance_uid.caption: Instance ID
instance_uid.description: The native session identifier of this invocation.

product.caption: Product
product.description: The CLI product and version that produced the observed records.

agentic_cli/content_block.caption: Content Block
agentic_cli/content_block.description: One ordered content block of a message. data holds the exact native block.
agentic_cli/content_block.name: content_block

block_index.caption: Block Index
block_index.description: Zero-based position of the block within the source record's content array.

block_type.caption: Block Type
block_type.description: The native block type string, exactly as reported.

block_kind_id.caption: Block Kind ID
block_kind_id.description: ACP-style content kind of the block, assigned by a declared mapping rule.

reasoning_form_id.caption: Reasoning Form ID
reasoning_form_id.description: What a reasoning content block holds, as a declared rule establishes it from the source. Absent when the source does not establish it.

1.caption: Full reasoning
1.description: The model's reasoning text as produced.

2.caption: Summary
2.description: A summary of the model's reasoning, not its full text.

text.caption: Text
text.description: The text content of a block when the source reports text.

tool_call_uid.caption: Tool Call ID
tool_call_uid.description: The native identifier of the tool call request. Absent when the source does not report one for the record.

data.caption: Data
data.description: The native block exactly as reported.

agentic_cli/cost_observation.caption: Cost Observation
agentic_cli/cost_observation.description: A reported cost total with its scope, currency, basis and source. Present only when a source reported a cost.
agentic_cli/cost_observation.name: cost_observation

total_cost.caption: Total Cost
total_cost.description: The reported cost total exactly as reported.

currency.caption: Currency
currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code of the reported cost.

scope_id.caption: Scope ID
scope_id.description: The scope at which the source reported this observation.

cost_basis.caption: Cost Basis
cost_basis.description: The source's reported pricing basis, if any (for example list).

source_ref.caption: Source Reference
source_ref.description: Which native source artifact and record occurrence supplied the facts in this event or object.

data.caption: Data
data.description: The native cost-bearing value or object exactly as reported.

agentic_cli/journal_provenance.caption: Journal Provenance
agentic_cli/journal_provenance.description: Agent Journal's provenance for a transformed or generated event. Invariant per-run facts (producer, capture time, contract hash) are stored once in run.json under shared and are reached through run_uid and contract_uid; they appear on an event only in a self-contained export.
agentic_cli/journal_provenance.name: journal_provenance

run_uid.caption: Journal Run ID
run_uid.description: The Agent Journal run identifier that owns this event.

invocation_index.caption: Invocation Index
invocation_index.description: Zero-based index of the CLI invocation within the Journal run.

sequence.caption: Sequence Number
sequence.description: Journal's event sequence within the run; occurrence order, never clock order.

producer.caption: Producer
producer.description: The Journal producer (transformer) that wrote the event; distinct from the originating CLI in metadata.product.

contract_uid.caption: Mapping Contract ID
contract_uid.description: Identifier of the mapping contract that produced this event, resolved through run.json.

rule_uid.caption: Mapping Rule ID
rule_uid.description: The contract rule that produced this event (0.5.0-prototype; earlier packages carry unmapped.rule_id).

contract_sha256.caption: Mapping Contract SHA-256
contract_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the mapping contract document embedded in run.json.

capture_time.caption: Capture Time
capture_time.description: When Journal observed or transformed the record, as epoch milliseconds.

capture_time_text.caption: Capture Time Text
capture_time_text.description: Journal's capture/transformation time at full precision, RFC 3339.

time_basis_id.caption: Time Basis ID
time_basis_id.description: How the event's time was established.

1.caption: Source record
1.description: The source record reports a timestamp; time is that value and metadata.original_time holds its text.

2.caption: Earliest available fallback
2.description: The record reports no time; time is the latest preceding source-reported time in the same occurrence sequence, or the capture start when none precedes. basis names which.

3.caption: Capture observation
3.description: The event is a Journal observation; time is when Journal observed it.

basis.caption: Basis
basis.description: Detail for the time basis (for example which preceding record supplied the fallback time).

capture_time_dt.caption: Capture Time
capture_time_dt.description: When Journal observed or transformed the record, as epoch milliseconds.

agentic_cli/model_ref.caption: Model Reference
agentic_cli/model_ref.description: Minimal reference to the reported model. Core ai_model requires a provider organization, which the admitted sources do not report per response; this object records provider information only with its basis.
agentic_cli/model_ref.name: model_ref

name.caption: Name
name.description: The model identifier exactly as reported.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The model version string, only when the source reports one separately from the model name.

provider_kind.caption: Provider Kind
provider_kind.description: A provider classification the source reported (for example firstParty). Not an organization name.

provider_basis_id.caption: Provider Basis ID
provider_basis_id.description: Whether provider information was reported, derived or is unavailable.

agentic_cli/operation.caption: Operation
agentic_cli/operation.description: A separately reported operation with its own identity and observed outcome. Its attribution states whether the source establishes a wrapping tool call: an operation the source reports on its own is a standalone observation, attributed Unattributed at its reported scope, never given an invented owner.
agentic_cli/operation.name: operation

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The operation's native identifier.

identity_basis_id.caption: Identity Basis ID
identity_basis_id.description: What kind of identifier the source reported as this fact's identity: tool_call_uid on a tool_call event, uid on an operation. A stream-local item identifier is not the identifier the model used for the call and cannot be joined with one.

1.caption: Model-facing call identifier
1.description: The identifier the model's own tool request carried, as the source reports it.

2.caption: Stream-local item identifier
2.description: An identifier the CLI's output stream assigns to its own items; unique within that stream only; the model-facing call identifier is not reported.

argv.caption: Command Vector
argv.description: The command as an argument vector when the source reports it that way.

command_line.caption: Command Line
command_line.description: The command exactly as the source reported it, as one string. Never parsed into argv; a shell's interpretation of it is not reported by this attribute.

exit_code.caption: Exit Code
exit_code.description: The exit code reported by a process when it terminates. The convention is that zero indicates success and any non-zero exit code indicates that some error occurred.

reported_state.caption: Reported State
reported_state.description: The lifecycle state string exactly as the source reported it (for example DONE, completed, failed).

attribution.caption: Attribution
attribution.description: How this fact was associated with its owner, with the declared outcome, candidates and basis.

data.caption: Data
data.description: The native operation record exactly as reported.

agentic_cli/permission_decision.caption: Permission Decision
agentic_cli/permission_decision.description: A permission decision at its reported scope. A decision reported without a reference to a tool call is retained at run or turn scope with an unattributed or ambiguous attribution; it is never attached to a tool call by guess.
agentic_cli/permission_decision.name: permission_decision

decision_id.caption: Decision ID
decision_id.description: Normalized permission decision. The core sibling decision carries the caption; reported_decision carries the source's own label.

decision.caption: Authorization Decision/Outcome
decision.description: Decision/outcome of the authorization mechanism (e.g. Approved, Denied)

reported_decision.caption: Reported Decision
reported_decision.description: The source's own decision label exactly as reported (for example accept, denied). decision carries the normalized caption.

decision_source.caption: Decision Source
decision_source.description: Who or what made the decision, as reported (for example config, user, cli).

reason_type.caption: Reason Type
reason_type.description: The reason category reported with the decision.

scope_id.caption: Scope ID
scope_id.description: The scope at which the source reported this observation.

attribution.caption: Attribution
attribution.description: How this fact was associated with its owner, with the declared outcome, candidates and basis.

source_ref.caption: Source Reference
source_ref.description: Which native source artifact and record occurrence supplied the facts in this event or object.

data.caption: Data
data.description: The native decision record exactly as reported.

agentic_cli/session_settings.caption: Session Settings
agentic_cli/session_settings.description: Launch/session settings as one native record reports them. Every attribute is optional: only reported values are present; nothing is defaulted or inferred.
agentic_cli/session_settings.name: session_settings

working_directory.caption: Working Directory
working_directory.description: The working directory the CLI reported.

model.caption: Model
model.description: The model identifier the CLI reported as configured.

provider.caption: Provider
provider.description: The model provider the CLI reported (a reported string, not an inferred organization).

version.caption: Version
version.description: The CLI version the record itself reports.

permission_mode.caption: Permission Mode
permission_mode.description: The CLI's reported permission/approval mode string exactly as reported (for example default, acceptEdits).

approval_policy.caption: Approval Policy
approval_policy.description: The CLI's reported approval policy string exactly as reported (for example never, on-request).

sandbox_policy.caption: Sandbox Policy
sandbox_policy.description: The CLI's reported sandbox policy exactly as reported (string or object).

tool_names.caption: Tool Names
tool_names.description: The tool names the CLI reported as available, in reported order.

git_branch.caption: Git Branch
git_branch.description: The git branch the CLI reported for the working directory.

agentic_cli/source_ref.caption: Source Reference
agentic_cli/source_ref.description: Identifies the native artifact and record occurrence that supplied a fact. The artifact hash is stored once per run in run.json sources and reached through artifact; it appears here only in a self-contained export.
agentic_cli/source_ref.name: source_ref

source_kind_id.caption: Source Kind ID
source_kind_id.description: Whether the artifact is live CLI output or a saved native session file.

artifact.caption: Artifact
artifact.description: Name of the source artifact within the run's source inventory.

artifact_sha256.caption: Artifact SHA-256
artifact_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the complete source artifact bytes.

record_index.caption: Record Index
record_index.description: One-based occurrence index of the record (line) within the artifact. This is the occurrence identity; native ids may repeat or be absent.

native_uid.caption: Native Record ID
native_uid.description: The record's own identifier when the source reports one.

native_time.caption: Native Time Text
native_time.description: The record's timestamp text verbatim, when reported.

record_bytes.caption: Record Bytes
record_bytes.description: Byte length of the record line excluding the line terminator.

line_ending.caption: Line Ending
line_ending.description: The line terminator observed after the record: LF, CRLF or none (last line without terminator).

is_whole_record.caption: Is Whole Record
is_whole_record.description: True when the event's data attribute holds the complete native record; false when it holds a fragment (for example one block). Reconstruction uses whole-record events only.

agentic_cli/tool_result.caption: Tool Result
agentic_cli/tool_result.description: The result returned for a tool call as the source reported it.
agentic_cli/tool_result.name: tool_result

data.caption: Data
data.description: The model-visible result content exactly as reported (string, array or object).

error_reported.caption: Error Reported
error_reported.description: Whether the source explicitly flagged the result as an error. Absent when the source reports nothing.

structured_result.caption: Structured Result
structured_result.description: Structured result detail the CLI reported beside the model-visible content (for example Claude's tool_use_result).

reported_state.caption: Reported State
reported_state.description: The lifecycle state string exactly as the source reported it (for example DONE, completed, failed).

agentic_cli/usage_observation.caption: Usage Observation
agentic_cli/usage_observation.description: One reported token-usage observation. Components are present only when reported; absence is not zero.
agentic_cli/usage_observation.name: usage_observation

scope_id.caption: Scope ID
scope_id.description: The scope at which the source reported this observation.

usage_status_id.caption: Usage Status ID
usage_status_id.description: Whether the reported usage is provisional or final, as established by the declared rule in basis.

basis.caption: Basis
basis.description: The declared rule that established usage_status_id.

source_ref.caption: Source Reference
source_ref.description: Which native source artifact and record occurrence supplied the facts in this event or object.

model_ref.caption: Model Reference
model_ref.description: Minimal reported-model reference. Used instead of core ai_model when the source does not report a provider organization.

reported_total_tokens.caption: Reported Total Tokens
reported_total_tokens.description: A total token figure only when the source reported it as a total. Never computed.

measurement_status_id.caption: Measurement Status ID
measurement_status_id.description: Whether the source establishes that the reported components are a measurement. Absent when no declared rule states it.

1.caption: Measured
1.description: The source reports these exact values only from a measurement.

2.caption: Possibly default
2.description: The source emits exactly these values also when it has no measurement (for example all-zero defaults); a measured value is not established.

data.caption: Data
data.description: The native usage object exactly as reported.

ai_agent.caption: AI Agent
ai_agent.description: An autonomous AI agent that performs tasks under delegated authority. Distinguished from the OCSF agent object (which describes security sensors such as EDR and DLP tools) and from human principals. An AI agent has a stable logical identity across runs and a restart-sensitive instance identity. The agent owns its model; the ai_model attribute captures which model was backing the agent at the time of action.
ai_agent.name: ai_agent

name.caption: Name
name.description: Human-readable name for the agent. For example: Q4 Analysis Agent or Model Tester Agent.

uid.caption: AI Agent ID
uid.description: The stable logical identifier for the agent, assigned by the agent's authoritative source (e.g., its control plane, registry, or issuing identity provider). Persists across restarts and instances. Producers populate this from whatever identity they observe: for a runtime that owns the agent, this is its issued ID; for a gateway or proxy, it is typically derived from the agent's credential. Multiple producers logging the same agent should converge on the same uid when they share an authoritative source.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

ai_model.caption: AI Model
ai_model.description: The AI model backing this agent at the time of the recorded event. An agent's model may change across instances or versions; this captures the model in use for the specific logged activity or delegation.

charter.caption: Agent Charter
charter.description: A document that defines an AI agent's durable role, responsibilities, constraints, and operating boundaries. When available, populate hashes on the file for content integrity and signatures for provenance. Integrity of the event that reports this agent is provided separately by the record_integrity profile.

instance_uid.caption: AI Agent Instance ID
instance_uid.description: Identifier for a specific running instance or session of the agent, distinct from the stable logical uid. An instance is a single materialization of the agent: a conversation, session, or run. It may persist across restarts (a session that is suspended and later resumed keeps the same instance_uid) and may span multiple cooperating runtime components, so several events can share one instance_uid. Enables attribution of actions to a particular instance of the agent rather than to the agent generally.

type.caption: Agent Type
type.description: The agent framework, normalized to the caption of the type_id value.

type_id.caption: Agent Type ID
type_id.description: The normalized identifier for the agent framework. Different agent frameworks have different identity, tool-call, and delegation semantics, so recording the framework enables cross-framework normalization. Communication protocols (e.g., MCP, A2A) are a property of individual operations rather than the agent itself, and are surfaced on the relevant operation rather than here.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The agent framework is not listed. Use the type attribute to describe it.

1.caption: Native
1.description: A first-party or proprietary agent built without a third-party agent framework. For example, a custom orchestrator or an LLM provider's own agent SDK.

2.caption: LangChain
2.description: An agent built with the LangChain framework.

3.caption: AutoGen
3.description: An agent built with the AutoGen framework for multi-agent conversation and orchestration.

4.caption: CrewAI
4.description: An agent built with the CrewAI framework for role-based multi-agent collaboration.

version.caption: AI Agent Version
version.description: The version of the agent: the agent's own code or configuration revision (e.g., 1.4.2), distinct from the version of the model backing it (carried on ai_model.version). Enables correlation of behavioral changes with charter or configuration revisions across agent versions.

ai_model.caption: AI Model
ai_model.description: The AI Model object describes the characteristics of an AI/ML model. Examples include language models like GPT-4, embedding models like text-embedding-ada-002, and computer vision models like CLIP.
ai_model.name: ai_model

name.caption: Name
name.description: Human-readable model name. For example: gpt-4o, claude-3-sonnet, or text-embedding-ada-002.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the AI model.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

ai_provider.caption: AI Provider
ai_provider.description: AI service provider or organization name. For example: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or Internal.

version.caption: Version

analytic.caption: Analytic
analytic.description: The Analytic object contains details about the analytic technique used to analyze and derive insights from the data or information that led to the creation of a finding or conclusion.

uid.caption: Unique ID

uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.

sensor_info_list.description: An array of sensor_info objects, each describing a sensor control point analyzed or correlated by the analytic. Each element typically represents a source of related_events that contributed to the finding. An individual sensor control point may also directly originate the finding, though more commonly it emits alerts that a downstream consumer treats as findings.

99.description: The state is not mapped. See the state attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

1.caption: Active
1.description: The Analytic is active.

2.caption: Suppressed
2.description: The Analytic is suppressed. For example, a user/customer has suppressed a particular detection signature in a security product.

3.caption: Experimental

type.caption: Type
type.description: The analytic type.

99.caption: Other

1.caption: Rule
1.description: A Rule in security analytics refers to predefined criteria or conditions set to monitor, alert, or enforce policies, playing a crucial role in access control, threat detection, and regulatory compliance across security systems.

2.caption: Behavioral
2.description: Behavioral analytics focus on monitoring and analyzing user or system actions to identify deviations from established patterns, aiding in the detection of insider threats, fraud, and advanced persistent threats (APTs).

3.caption: Statistical
3.description: Statistical analytics pertains to analyzing data patterns and anomalies using statistical models to predict, detect, and respond to potential threats, enhancing overall security posture through informed decision-making.

4.caption: Learning (ML/DL)
4.description: Learning (ML/DL) encompasses techniques that can "learn" from known data to create analytics that generalize to new data. There may be a statistical component to these techniques, but it is not a requirement.

5.caption: Fingerprinting
5.description: Fingerprinting is the technique of collecting detailed system data, including software versions and configurations, to enhance threat detection, data loss prevention (DLP), and endpoint detection and response (EDR) capabilities.

6.caption: Tagging
6.description: Tagging refers to the practice of assigning labels or identifiers to data, users, assets, or activities to monitor, control access, and facilitate incident response across various security domains such as DLP and EDR.

7.caption: Keyword Match
7.description: Keyword Match involves scanning content for specific terms to identify sensitive information, potential threats, or policy violations, aiding in DLP and compliance monitoring.

8.caption: Regular Expressions
8.description: Regular Expressions are used to define complex search patterns for identifying, validating, and extracting specific data sets or threats within digital content, enhancing DLP, EDR, and threat detection mechanisms.

9.caption: Exact Data Match
9.description: Exact Data Match is a precise comparison technique used to detect the unauthorized use or exposure of specific, sensitive information, crucial for enforcing DLP policies and protecting against data breaches.

10.caption: Partial Data Match
10.description: Partial Data Match involves identifying instances where segments of sensitive information or patterns match, facilitating nuanced DLP and threat detection without requiring complete data conformity.

11.caption: Indexed Data Match
11.description: Indexed Data Match refers to comparing content against a pre-compiled index of sensitive information to efficiently detect and prevent unauthorized access or breaches, streamlining DLP and compliance efforts.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The analytic version. For example: 1.1.

tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the application.

type.description: The type of application as defined by the event source, e.g., GitHub, Azure Logic App, or Amazon Elastic BeanStalk.

uid_alt.caption: Application Alternative ID
uid_alt.description: An alternative or contextual identifier for the application, such as a configuration, organization, or license UID.

version.caption: Application Version
