cores.caption: Cores
cores.description: The number of processing cores or compute units for the component.

model.caption: Model
model.description: The model name of the GPU. For example: GeForce RTX A6000, Radeon PRO W7900, or Intel Data Center GPU Max 1550.

vendor_name.caption: Vendor Name
vendor_name.description: The name of the vendor of the GPU. For example: NVIDIA, AMD, or Intel.

vram_mode.caption: VRAM Mode
vram_mode.description: The video memory attachment mode, indicating how the VRAM hardware is integrated with the system (e.g., shared or dedicated), normalized to the caption of the vram_mode_id value. For 'Other', the exact attachment mode is defined by the event source.

vram_mode_id.caption: VRAM Mode ID
vram_mode_id.description: The normalized identifier of the video memory attachment mode.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The VRAM mode is unknown or not reported.

1.caption: Shared
1.description: Video memory is allocated from system memory.

2.caption: Dedicated
2.description: Video memory is physically separate from system memory.

99.caption: Other
99.description: A VRAM mode not covered by the defined values; the exact value is reported by the event source.

vram_size.caption: VRAM Size
vram_size.description: The total amount of installed video RAM.

graph.caption: Graph
graph.description: A graph data structure representation with nodes and edges.
graph.name: graph

name.caption: Name
name.description: The graph name - a human readable identifier for the graph.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: Unique identifier of the graph - a unique ID to reference this specific graph.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The graph description - provides additional details about the graph's purpose and contents.

edges.caption: Edges
edges.description: The edges/connections between nodes in the graph - contains the collection of edge objects defining relationships between nodes.

is_directed.caption: Directed
is_directed.description: Indicates if the graph is directed (true) or undirected (false).

nodes.caption: Nodes
nodes.description: The nodes/vertices of the graph - contains the collection of node objects that make up the graph.

query_language.caption: Query Language
query_language.description: The graph query language, normalized to the caption of the query_language_id value.

query_language_id.caption: Query Language ID
query_language_id.description: The normalized identifier of a graph query language that can be used to interact with the graph.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The Query Language is not mapped. See the query_language attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

1.caption: Cypher
1.description: A declarative graph query language developed by Neo4j that allows for expressive and efficient querying of graph databases.

2.caption: GraphQL
2.description: A query language for APIs that enables declarative data fetching and provides a complete description of the data in the API.

3.caption: Gremlin
3.description: A graph traversal language and virtual machine developed by Apache TinkerPop that enables graph computing across different graph databases.

4.caption: GQL
4.description: An ISO standard graph query language designed to provide a unified way to query graph databases.

5.caption: G-CORE
5.description: A graph query language that combines features from existing languages while adding support for paths as first-class citizens.

6.caption: PGQL
6.description: Property Graph Query Language developed by Oracle that provides SQL-like syntax for querying property graphs.

7.caption: SPARQL
7.description: A semantic query language for databases that enables querying and manipulating data stored in RDF format.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The graph type. Typically useful to represent the specific type of graph that is used.

group.caption: Group
group.description: The Group object represents a collection or association of entities, such as users, policies, or devices. It serves as a logical grouping mechanism to organize and manage entities with similar characteristics or permissions within a system or organization, including but not limited to purposes of access control.
group.name: group

name.caption: Name
name.description: The group name.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the group. For example, for Windows events this is the security identifier (SID) of the group. Another example, pool id or desktop id that the device belongs to.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

domain.caption: Domain
domain.description: The domain where the group is defined. For example: the LDAP or Active Directory domain.

type.caption: Group Type
type.description: The type of the group.

http_header.caption: HTTP Header
http_header.description: The HTTP Header object represents the headers sent in an HTTP request or response. HTTP headers are key-value pairs that convey additional information about the HTTP message, including details about the content, caching, authentication, encoding, and other aspects of the communication.
http_header.name: http_header

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the HTTP header.

value.caption: Value
value.description: The value of the HTTP header.

iam_role.caption: IAM Role
iam_role.description: The IAM Role object describes permission characteristics (or privileges) associated with a user or group of users as security principals against one or more resources. In some cases only the name or ID of the role is known hence other attributes are optional. In some systems a user or group of users can have multiple roles, imparting the union of privileges to the principal. In some systems the role can serve as a temporary security principal without its own credentials on behalf of the actual security principal.
iam_role.name: iam_role

name.caption: Name
name.description: The role name. For example, Power Users.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique role identifier. For example, the Windows role SID, or AWS role ARN.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

account.caption: Account
account.description: The account associated with the role. For example, can be a cross-account role, different from the user or group account, granting access within this account.

policies.caption: Policies
policies.description: IAM policies associated with the role.

privileges.caption: Privileges
privileges.description: List of privileges assigned to a role.

programmatic_credentials.caption: Programmatic Credentials
programmatic_credentials.description: Programmatic credential (API keys, access tokens, certificates, etc) associated with the role.

resources.caption: Resources Array
resources.description: Resources that the role applies to.

session.caption: Session
session.description: The session where the role is active. Some roles may be temporary and expire when the session expires.

uid_alt.caption: Alternate ID
uid_alt.description: The alternate user identifier. For example, the Active Directory role GUID or the associated LDAP group DN.

idp.caption: Identity Provider
idp.description: The Identity Provider object contains detailed information about a provider responsible for creating, maintaining, and managing identity information while offering authentication services to applications. An Identity Provider (IdP) serves as a trusted authority that verifies the identity of users and issues authentication tokens or assertions to enable secure access to applications or services.
idp.name: idp

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the Identity Provider.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the Identity Provider.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

auth_factors.caption: Authentication Factors
auth_factors.description: The Authentication Factors object describes the different types of Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) methods and/or devices supported by the Identity Provider.

domain.caption: Domain
domain.description: The primary domain associated with the Identity Provider.

fingerprint.caption: Certificate Fingerprint
fingerprint.description: The fingerprint of the X.509 certificate used by the Identity Provider.

has_mfa.caption: MFA Enforced
has_mfa.description: The Identity Provider enforces Multi Factor Authentication (MFA).

issuer.caption: Issuer Details
issuer.description: The unique identifier (often a URL) used by the Identity Provider as its issuer.

protocol_name.caption: Supported Protocol
protocol_name.description: The supported protocol of the Identity Provider. E.g., SAML, OIDC, or OAuth2.

scim.caption: SCIM
scim.description: The System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) resource object as defined in RFC 7634 provides a structured set of attributes related to SCIM protocols used for identity provisioning and management across cloud-based platforms. It standardizes user and group provisioning details, enabling identity synchronization and lifecycle management with compatible Identity Providers (IdPs) and applications.

sso.caption: SSO
sso.description: The Single Sign-On (SSO) object provides a structure for normalizing SSO attributes, configuration, and/or settings from Identity Providers.

state.caption: State
state.description: The configuration state of the Identity Provider, normalized to the caption of the state_id value. In the case of Other, it is defined by the event source.

state_id.caption: State ID
state_id.description: The normalized state ID of the Identity Provider to reflect its configuration or activation status.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The configuration state of the Identity Provider is unknown.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The configuration state of the Identity Provider is not mapped. See the state attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

1.caption: Active
1.description: The Identity Provider is in an Active state, or otherwise enabled.

2.caption: Suspended
2.description: The Identity Provider is in a Suspended state.

3.caption: Deprecated
3.description: The Identity Provider is in a Deprecated state, or is otherwise disabled.

4.caption: Deleted
4.description: The Identity Provider is in a Deleted state.

tenant_uid.caption: Tenant UID
tenant_uid.description: The tenant ID associated with the Identity Provider.

url_string.caption: Configuration URL
url_string.description: The URL for accessing the configuration or metadata of the Identity Provider.

image.caption: Image
image.description: The Image object provides a description of a specific Virtual Machine (VM) or Container image.
image.name: image

name.caption: Name
name.description: The image name. For example: elixir.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique image ID. For example: 77af4d6b9913.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The list of labels associated to the image.

path.caption: Path
path.description: The full path to the image file.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the image.

kb_article.caption: KB Article
kb_article.description: The KB Article object contains metadata that describes the patch or update.
kb_article.name: kb_article

classification.caption: Classification
classification.description: The vendors classification of the kb article.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The date the kb article was released by the vendor.

install_state.caption: Install State
install_state.description: The install state of the kb article.

install_state_id.caption: Install State ID
install_state_id.description: The normalized install state ID of the kb article.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The normalized install state is unknown.

1.caption: Installed
1.description: The item is installed.

2.caption: Not Installed
2.description: The item is not installed.

3.caption: Installed Pending Reboot
3.description: The item is installed pending reboot operation.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The install state is not mapped. See the install_state attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

is_superseded.caption: The patch is superseded.
is_superseded.description: The kb article has been replaced by another.

os.caption: OS
os.description: The operating system the kb article applies.

product.caption: Product
product.description: The product details the kb article applies.

severity.caption: Severity
severity.description: The severity of the kb article.

size.caption: Size
size.description: The size in bytes for the kb article.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The kb article link from the source vendor.

title.caption: Title
title.description: The title of the kb article.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier for the kb article.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time
created_time_dt.description: The date the kb article was released by the vendor.

key_value_object.caption: Key:Value object
key_value_object.description: A generic object allowing to define a {key:value} pair.
key_value_object.name: key_value_object

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the key.

value.caption: Value
value.description: The value associated to the key.

values.caption: Values
values.description: Optional, the values associated to the key. You can populate this attribute, when you have multiple values for the same key.

keyboard_info.caption: Keyboard Information
keyboard_info.description: The Keyboard Information object contains details and attributes related to a computer or device keyboard. It encompasses information that describes the characteristics, capabilities, and configuration of the keyboard.
keyboard_info.name: keyboard_info

function_keys.caption: Function Keys
function_keys.description: The number of function keys on client keyboard.

ime.caption: IME
ime.description: The Input Method Editor (IME) file name.

keyboard_layout.caption: Keyboard Layout
keyboard_layout.description: The keyboard locale identifier name (e.g., en-US).

kill_chain_phase.caption: Kill Chain Phase
kill_chain_phase.description: The Kill Chain Phase object represents a single phase of a cyber attack, including the initial reconnaissance and planning stages up to the final objective of the attacker. It provides a detailed description of each phase and its associated activities within the broader context of a cyber attack.
kill_chain_phase.name: kill_chain_phase

phase_id.caption: Kill Chain Phase ID
phase_id.description: The cyber kill chain phase identifier.

0.caption: Unknown
0.description: The kill chain phase is unknown.

1.caption: Reconnaissance
1.description: The attackers pick a target and perform a detailed analysis, start collecting information (email addresses, conferences information, etc.) and evaluate the victim’s vulnerabilities to determine how to exploit them.

2.caption: Weaponization
2.description: The attackers develop a malware weapon and aim to exploit the discovered vulnerabilities.

3.caption: Delivery
3.description: The intruders will use various tactics, such as phishing, infected USB drives, etc.

4.caption: Exploitation
4.description: The intruders start leveraging vulnerabilities to executed code on the victim’s system.

5.caption: Installation
5.description: The intruders install malware on the victim’s system.

6.caption: Command & Control
6.description: Malware opens a command channel to enable the intruders to remotely manipulate the victim's system.

7.caption: Actions on Objectives
7.description: With hands-on keyboard access, intruders accomplish the mission’s goal.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The kill chain phase is not mapped. See the phase attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

ldap_person.caption: LDAP Person
ldap_person.description: The additional LDAP attributes that describe a person.
ldap_person.name: ldap_person

cost_center.caption: Cost Center
cost_center.description: The cost center associated with the user.

created_time.caption: Created Time
created_time.description: The timestamp when the user was created.

deleted_time.caption: Deleted Time
deleted_time.description: The timestamp when the user was deleted. In Active Directory (AD), when a user is deleted they are moved to a temporary container and then removed after 30 days. So, this field can be populated even after a user is deleted for the next 30 days.

department.caption: Department
department.description: The name of the department in which the user works.

display_name.caption: Display Name
display_name.description: The display name of the LDAP person. According to RFC 2798, this is the preferred name of a person to be used when displaying entries.

email_addrs.caption: Email Addresses
email_addrs.description: A list of additional email addresses for the user.

employee_uid.caption: Employee ID
employee_uid.description: The employee identifier assigned to the user by the organization.

given_name.caption: Given Name
given_name.description: The given or first name of the user.

hire_time.caption: Hire Time
hire_time.description: The timestamp when the user was or will be hired by the organization.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The labels associated with the user. For example in AD this could be the userType, employeeType. For example: Member, Employee.

last_login_time.caption: Last Login
last_login_time.description: The last time when the user logged in.

ldap_cn.caption: LDAP Common Name
ldap_cn.description: The LDAP and X.500 commonName attribute, typically the full name of the person. For example, John Doe.

ldap_dn.caption: LDAP Distinguished Name
ldap_dn.description: The X.500 Distinguished Name (DN) is a structured string that uniquely identifies an entry, such as a user, in an X.500 directory service For example, cn=John Doe,ou=People,dc=example,dc=com.

leave_time.caption: Leave Time
leave_time.description: The timestamp when the user left or will be leaving the organization.

location.caption: Geo Location
location.description: The geographical location associated with a user. This is typically the user's usual work location.

manager.caption: Manager
manager.description: The user's manager. This helps in understanding an org hierarchy. This should only ever be populated once in an event. I.e. there should not be a manager's manager in an event.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The timestamp when the user entry was last modified.

office_location.caption: Office Location
office_location.description: The primary office location associated with the user. This could be any string and isn't a specific address. For example, South East Virtual.

phone_number.caption: Telephone Number
phone_number.description: The telephone number of the user. Corresponds to the LDAP Telephone-Number CN.

surname.caption: Surname
surname.description: The last or family name for the user.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the user.

created_time_dt.caption: Created Time
created_time_dt.description: The timestamp when the user was created.

deleted_time_dt.caption: Deleted Time
deleted_time_dt.description: The timestamp when the user was deleted. In Active Directory (AD), when a user is deleted they are moved to a temporary container and then removed after 30 days. So, this field can be populated even after a user is deleted for the next 30 days.

hire_time_dt.caption: Hire Time
hire_time_dt.description: The timestamp when the user was or will be hired by the organization.

last_login_time_dt.caption: Last Login
last_login_time_dt.description: The last time when the user logged in.

leave_time_dt.caption: Leave Time
leave_time_dt.description: The timestamp when the user left or will be leaving the organization.

modified_time_dt.caption: Modified Time
modified_time_dt.description: The timestamp when the user entry was last modified.

location.caption: Geo Location
location.description: The Geo Location object describes a geographical location, usually associated with an IP address.
location.name: location

aerial_height.caption: Aerial Height
aerial_height.description: Expressed as either height above takeoff location or height above ground level (AGL) for a UAS current location. This value is provided in meters and must have a minimum resolution of 1 m. Special Values: Invalid, No Value, or Unknown: -1000 m.

coordinates.caption: Coordinates
coordinates.description: A two-element array, containing a longitude/latitude pair. The format conforms with GeoJSON. For example: [-73.983, 40.719].

country.caption: Country
country.description:
The ISO 3166-1 Alpha-2 country code.

Note: The two letter country code should be capitalized. For example: US or CA.

desc.caption: Description
desc.description: The description of the geographical location.

geodetic_altitude.caption: Geodetic Altitude
geodetic_altitude.description: The aircraft distance above or below the ellipsoid as measured along a line that passes through the aircraft and is normal to the surface of the WGS-84 ellipsoid. This value is provided in meters and must have a minimum resolution of 1 m. Special Values: Invalid, No Value, or Unknown: -1000 m.

geodetic_vertical_accuracy.caption: Geodetic Vertical Accuracy
geodetic_vertical_accuracy.description: Provides quality/containment on geodetic altitude. This is based on ADS-B Geodetic Vertical Accuracy (GVA). Measured in meters.

geohash.caption: Geohash
geohash.description:
Geohash of the geo-coordinates (latitude and longitude).

Geohashing is a geocoding system used to encode geographic coordinates in decimal degrees, to a single string.

horizontal_accuracy.caption: Horizontal Accuracy
horizontal_accuracy.description: Provides quality/containment on horizontal position. This is based on ADS-B NACp. Measured in meters.

is_on_premises.caption: On-Premises
is_on_premises.description: Indicates whether the location is on-premises.

isp.caption: ISP Name
isp.description: The name of the Internet Service Provider (ISP).

@deprecated.message: Use the network_endpoint.isp or whois.isp attribute according to your use-case.

lat.caption: Latitude
lat.description: The geographical Latitude coordinate represented in Decimal Degrees (DD). For example: 42.361145.

long.caption: Longitude
long.description: The geographical Longitude coordinate represented in Decimal Degrees (DD). For example: -71.057083.

postal_code.caption: Postal Code
postal_code.description: The postal code of the location.

pressure_altitude.caption: Pressure Altitude
pressure_altitude.description: The uncorrected barometric pressure altitude (based on reference standard 29.92 inHg, 1013.25 mb) provides a reference for algorithms that utilize 'altitude deltas' between aircraft. This value is provided in meters and must have a minimum resolution of 1 m.. Special Values: Invalid, No Value, or Unknown: -1000 m.

provider.caption: Provider
provider.description: The provider of the geographical location data.

region.caption: Region
region.description: The alphanumeric code that identifies the principal subdivision (e.g. province or state) of the country. For example, 'CH-VD' for the Canton of Vaud, Switzerland

logger.caption: Logger
logger.description: The Logger object represents the device and product where events are stored with times for receipt and transmission.  This may be at the source device where the event occurred, a remote scanning device, intermediate hops, or the ultimate destination.
logger.name: logger

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the logging product instance.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the logging product instance.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

device.caption: Device
device.description: The device where the events are logged.

event_uid.caption: Event UID
event_uid.description: The unique identifier of the event assigned by the logger.

is_truncated.caption: Is Truncated
is_truncated.description: Indicates whether the OCSF event data has been truncated due to size limitations. When true, some event data may have been omitted to fit within system constraints.

log_format.caption: Log Format
log_format.description: The format of data in the log. For example JSON, syslog or CSV.

log_level.caption: Log Level
log_level.description: The level at which an event was logged. This can be log provider specific. For example the audit level.

log_name.caption: Log Name
log_name.description: The log name for the logging provider log, or the file name of the system log. This may be an intermediate store-and-forward log or a vendor destination log. For example /archive/server1/var/log/messages.0 or /var/log/.

log_provider.caption: Log Provider
log_provider.description: The logging provider or logging service that logged the event. This may be an intermediate application store-and-forward log or a vendor destination log.

log_version.caption: Log Version
log_version.description: The event log schema version of the original event. For example the syslog version or the Cisco Log Schema version

logged_time.caption: Logged Time
logged_time.description: The time when this logger received and logged the event. For the last logger in the pipeline, this value should match metadata.logged_time.

product.caption: Product
product.description: The product logging the event.  This may be the event source product, a management server product, a scanning product, a SIEM, etc.

transmit_time.caption: Transmission Time
transmit_time.description: The time when the event was transmitted from the logging device to it's next destination.

untruncated_size.caption: Untruncated Size
untruncated_size.description: The original size of the OCSF event data in kilobytes before any truncation occurred. This field is typically populated when is_truncated is true to indicate the full size of the original event.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the logging provider.

logged_time_dt.caption: Logged Time
logged_time_dt.description: The time when this logger received and logged the event. For the last logger in the pipeline, this value should match metadata.logged_time.

transmit_time_dt.caption: Transmission Time
transmit_time_dt.description: The time when the event was transmitted from the logging device to it's next destination.

long_string.caption: Long String
long_string.description: This object is a used to capture strings which may be truncated by a security product due to their length.
long_string.name: long_string

is_truncated.caption: Is Truncated
is_truncated.description: Indicates that value has been truncated. May be omitted if truncation has not occurred.

untruncated_size.caption: Untruncated Size
untruncated_size.description: The size in bytes of the string represented by value before truncation. Should be omitted if truncation has not occurred.

value.caption: Value
value.description: The string value, truncated if is_truncated is true.

malware.caption: Malware
malware.description: The Malware object describes the classification of known malicious software, which is intentionally designed to cause damage to a computer, server, client, or computer network.
malware.name: malware

name.caption: Name
name.description: The malware name, as reported by the detection engine.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: A unique identifier for the specific malware instance, as assigned by the detection engine (e.g., virus signature ID or IPS rule ID).

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

classification_ids.caption: Classification IDs
classification_ids.description: The list of normalized identifiers of the malware classifications.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The classification is not mapped. See the classifications attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

classifications.caption: Classifications
classifications.description: The list of malware classifications, normalized to the captions of the classification_ids values. In the case of 'Other', they are defined by the event source.

cves.caption: CVE List
cves.description: The list of Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) identifiers associated with the malware.

files.caption: Files
files.description: The list of file objects representing files that were identified as infected by the malware.

num_infected.caption: Number of Infected Entities
num_infected.description: The number of files that were identified to be infected by the malware.

path.caption: Path
path.description: The filesystem path of the malware that was observed.

provider.caption: Provider
provider.description: The name or identifier of the security solution or service that provided the malware detection information.

severity.caption: Severity
severity.description: The severity of the malware, normalized to the captions of the severity_id values. In the case of 'Other', they are defined by the event source.

severity_id.caption: Severity ID
severity_id.description: The normalized identifier of the malware severity.

1.caption: Informational
1.description: Informational message. No action required.

2.caption: Low
2.description: The user decides if action is needed.

3.caption: Medium
3.description: Action is required but the situation is not serious at this time.

4.caption: High
4.description: Action is required immediately.

5.caption: Critical
5.description: Action is required immediately and the scope is broad.

6.caption: Fatal
6.description: An error occurred but it is too late to take remedial action.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The event/finding severity is not mapped. See the severity attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

malware_scan_info.caption: Malware Scan Info
malware_scan_info.description: The malware scan information object describes characteristics, metadata of a malware scanning job.
malware_scan_info.name: malware_scan_info

name.caption: Name
name.description: The administrator-supplied or application-generated name of the scan. For example: "Home office weekly user database scan", "Scan folders for viruses", "Full system virus scan"

uid.caption: Scan UID
uid.description: The application-defined unique identifier assigned to an instance of a scan.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of scan.

type_id.caption: Type ID
type_id.description: The type id of the scan.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The scan type id is not mapped. See the type attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

1.caption: Manual
1.description: The scan was manually initiated by the user or administrator.

2.caption: Scheduled
2.description: The scan was started based on scheduler.

3.caption: Updated Content
3.description: The scan was triggered by a content update.

4.caption: Quarantined Items
4.description: The scan was triggered by newly quarantined items.

5.caption: Attached Media
5.description: The scan was triggered by the attachment of removable media.

6.caption: User Logon
6.description: The scan was started due to a user logon.

7.caption: ELAM
7.description: The scan was triggered by an Early Launch Anti-Malware (ELAM) detection.

end_time.caption: End Time

num_infected.caption: Number of Infected Entities

num_volumes.caption: Number of Volumes
num_volumes.description: The total number of storage volumes examined during the malware scan.

size.caption: Size

start_time.caption: Start Time
start_time.description: The timestamp indicating when the scan job began execution.

unique_malware_count.caption: Unique Malware Count

end_time_dt.caption: End Time
end_time_dt.description: The timestamp indicating when the scan job completed execution.

start_time_dt.caption: Start Time
start_time_dt.description: The timestamp indicating when the scan job began execution.

metadata.caption: Metadata
metadata.description: The Metadata object describes the metadata associated with the event.
metadata.name: metadata

data_classification.caption: Data Classification
data_classification.description: The Data Classification object includes information about data classification levels and data category types.

data_classifications.caption: Data Classification
data_classifications.description: A list of Data Classification objects, that include information about data classification levels and data category types, identified by a classifier.

correlation_uid.caption: Correlation UID
correlation_uid.description: A unique identifier used to correlate this OCSF event with other related OCSF events, distinct from the event's uid value. This enables linking multiple OCSF events that are part of the same activity, transaction, or security incident across different systems or time periods.

debug.caption: Debug Information
debug.description: Debug information about non-fatal issues with this OCSF event. Each issue is a line in this string array.

event_code.caption: Event Code
event_code.description: The identifier of the original event. For example the numerical Windows Event Code or Cisco syslog code.

extension.caption: Schema Extension
extension.description: The schema extension used to create the event.

extensions.caption: Schema Extensions
extensions.description: The schema extensions used to create the event.

is_truncated.caption: Is Truncated
is_truncated.description: Indicates whether the OCSF event data has been truncated due to size limitations. When true, some event data may have been omitted to fit within system constraints.

labels.caption: Labels
labels.description: The list of labels attached to the event. For example: ["sample", "dev"]

log_format.caption: Log Source Format
log_format.description: The format of data in the log where the data originated. For example CSV, XML, Windows Multiline, JSON, syslog or Cisco Log Schema.

log_level.caption: Log Level
log_level.description: The level at which an event was logged. This can be log provider specific. For example the audit level.

log_name.caption: Log Name
log_name.description: The event log name, typically for the consumer of the event. For example, the storage bucket name, SIEM repository index name, etc.

log_provider.caption: Log Provider
log_provider.description: The logging provider or logging service that logged the event. For example AWS CloudWatch or Splunk.

log_source.caption: Log Source
log_source.description: The log system or component where the data originated. For example, a file path, syslog server name or a Windows hostname and logging subsystem such as Security.

log_version.caption: Log Version
log_version.description: The event log schema version of the original event. For example the syslog version or the Cisco Log Schema version

logged_time.caption: Logged Time
logged_time.description: The ultimate logged time in the event pipeline - when the event reached its final destination (e.g., SIEM, data lake). If loggers is populated, this should match the logged_time of the last entry in the loggers array. This is distinct from time (when the activity occurred) and processed_time (when an intermediate system processed the event).

loggers.caption: Loggers
loggers.description: An ordered array of Logger objects describing each hop in the event pipeline between the source and its final destination. Each entry captures the logging product, device, and timestamps (logged_time, transmit_time) at that stage. The last entry's logged_time should match metadata.logged_time.

modified_time.caption: Modified Time
modified_time.description: The time when the event was last modified or enriched.

original_event_uid.caption: Original Event ID
original_event_uid.description: The unique identifier assigned to the event in its original logging system before transformation to OCSF format. This field preserves the source system's native event identifier, enabling traceability back to the raw log entry. For example, a Windows Event Record ID, a syslog message ID, a Splunk _cd value, or a database transaction log sequence number.

original_time.caption: Original Time
original_time.description: The original event time as reported by the event source, preserved as a pass-through string in its native format (e.g., Syslog timestamp, Windows event time). This is not normalized to timestamp_t - the normalized equivalent is the base event time attribute. Omit if the event is generated rather than collected via logs.

processed_time.caption: Processed Time
processed_time.description: The time when the event was processed by an intermediate system (e.g., ETL pipeline, event processor) before reaching its final destination. Can be used with logged_time to calculate queuing duration via total_queued_duration.

product.caption: Product
product.description: The product that reported the event.

profiles.caption: Profiles
profiles.description: The list of profiles used to create the event. Profiles should be referenced by their name attribute for core profiles, or extension/name for profiles from extensions.

reporter.caption: Reporter
reporter.description: The entity from which the event or finding was first reported.

sequence.caption: Sequence Number
sequence.description: Sequence number of the event. The sequence number is a value available in some events, to make the exact ordering of events unambiguous, regardless of the event time precision.

source.caption: Source
source.description: The source of the event or finding. This can be any distinguishing name for the logical origin of the data — for example, 'CloudTrail Events', or a use case like 'Attack Simulations' or 'Vulnerability Scans'.

tags.caption: Tags
tags.description: The list of tags; {key:value} pairs associated to the event.

total_queued_duration.caption: Total Queued Duration
total_queued_duration.description: The amount of time an event spent in a queue awaiting processing. In this case, the value is the difference between processed_time and logged_time. This duration is inclusive of all queues between the originator of the event and the intended long-term storage destination of the event.

transformation_info_list.caption: Transformation Info
transformation_info_list.description: An array of transformation info that describes the mappings or transforms applied to the data.

transmit_time.caption: Transmission Time
transmit_time.description: The time when the event was transmitted from the logging device to it's next destination.

type.caption: Type
type.description: The type of the event or finding as a subset of the source of the event. This can be any distinguishing characteristic of the data. For example 'Management Events' or 'Device Penetration Test'.

uid.caption: Event UID
uid.description: A unique identifier assigned to the OCSF event. This ID is specific to the OCSF event itself and is distinct from the original event identifier in the source system (see original_event_uid).

untruncated_size.caption: Untruncated Size
untruncated_size.description: The original size of the OCSF event data in kilobytes before any truncation occurred. This field is typically populated when is_truncated is true to indicate the full size of the original event.

version.caption: Version
version.description: The version of the OCSF schema, using Semantic Versioning Specification (SemVer). For example: 1.0.0. Event consumers use the version to determine the available event attributes.

logged_time_dt.caption: Logged Time
logged_time_dt.description: The ultimate logged time in the event pipeline - when the event reached its final destination (e.g., SIEM, data lake). If loggers is populated, this should match the logged_time of the last entry in the loggers array. This is distinct from time (when the activity occurred) and processed_time (when an intermediate system processed the event).

modified_time_dt.caption: Modified Time
modified_time_dt.description: The time when the event was last modified or enriched.

processed_time_dt.caption: Processed Time
processed_time_dt.description: The time when the event was processed by an intermediate system (e.g., ETL pipeline, event processor) before reaching its final destination. Can be used with logged_time to calculate queuing duration via total_queued_duration.

transmit_time_dt.caption: Transmission Time
transmit_time_dt.description: The time when the event was transmitted from the logging device to it's next destination.

metric.caption: Metric
metric.description: The Metric object defines a simple name/value pair entity for a metric.
metric.name: metric

name.caption: Name
name.description: The name of the metric.

mitigation.caption: MITRE Mitigation
mitigation.description: The MITRE Mitigation object describes the ATT&CK® or ATLAS™ Mitigation ID and/or name that is associated to an attack.
mitigation.name: mitigation

name.caption: Name
name.description: The Mitigation name that is associated with the attack technique. For example: Password Policies, or Code Signing.

uid.caption: Unique ID
uid.description: The Mitigation ID that is associated with the attack technique. For example: M1027, or AML.M0013.

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID
uid_numeric.description:
The uid attribute in numeric form where applicable.
Note: Producers may populate uid_numeric only in addition to uid and not as an alternative to it.

countermeasures.caption: Countermeasures
countermeasures.description: The D3FEND countermeasures that are associated with the attack technique. For example: ATT&CK Technique T1003 is addressed by Mitigation M1027, and D3FEND Technique D3-OTP.

src_url.caption: Source URL
src_url.description: The versioned permalink of the Mitigation. For example: https://attack.mitre.org/versions/v14/mitigations/M1027.

references.description: ATT&CK® Mitigation to D3FEND™ Technique Mappings

network_endpoint.description: The Network Endpoint object describes characteristics of a network endpoint. These can be a source or destination of a network connection.
network_endpoint.name: network_endpoint

name.caption: Name
name.description: The short name of the endpoint.

uid.caption: Unique ID

uid_numeric.caption: Numeric Unique ID

container.description: The information describing an instance of a container. A container is a prepackaged, portable system image that runs isolated on an existing system using a container runtime like containerd.

namespace_pid.description: If running under a process namespace (such as in a container), the process identifier within that process namespace.

hostname.caption: Hostname
hostname.description: The fully qualified name of the endpoint.

instance_uid.description: The unique identifier of a VM instance.

interface_name.description: The name of the network interface (e.g. eth2).

interface_uid.caption: Network Interface ID
interface_uid.description: The unique identifier of the network interface.

ip.caption: IP Address
ip.description: The IP address of the endpoint, in either IPv4 or IPv6 format.

location.caption: Geo Location
location.description: The geographical location of the endpoint.

mac.caption: MAC Address
mac.description: The Media Access Control (MAC) address of the endpoint.

mac_vendor.description: The vendor or manufacturer of the endpoint's network interface controller (NIC), as identified from the MAC address.

owner.caption: Owner
owner.description: The identity of the service or user account that owns the endpoint or was last logged into it.

pool.caption: Pool
pool.description: The pool of desktops or virtual machines to which the endpoint belongs.

subnet_uid.caption: Subnet UID
subnet_uid.description: The unique identifier of a virtual subnet.

vpc_uid.caption: VPC UID
vpc_uid.description: The unique identifier of the Virtual Private Cloud (VPC).

zone.caption: Network Zone

autonomous_system.caption: Autonomous System
autonomous_system.description: The Autonomous System details associated with an IP address.

fingerprints.caption: Fingerprints
fingerprints.description: Fingerprints that identify the specific application implementation on this endpoint, such as Cisco NPF or HASSH.

intermediate_ips.caption: Intermediate IP Addresses
intermediate_ips.description: The intermediate IP Addresses. For example, the IP addresses in the HTTP X-Forwarded-For header.

isp.caption: ISP Name
isp.description: The name of the Internet Service Provider (ISP).

isp_org.caption: ISP Org
isp_org.description: The organization name of the Internet Service Provider (ISP). This represents the parent organization or company that owns/operates the ISP. For example, Comcast Corporation would be the ISP org for Xfinity internet service. This attribute helps identify the ultimate provider when ISPs operate under different brand names.

network_scope.caption: Network Scope
network_scope.description: Indicates whether the endpoint resides inside the customer’s network, outside on the Internet, or if its location relative to the customer’s network cannot be determined. The value is normalized to the caption of the network_scope_id.

network_scope_id.caption: Network Scope ID
network_scope_id.description: The normalized identifier of the endpoint’s network scope. 0.description: Unknown whether this endpoint resides within the customer’s network.

1.description: The endpoint resides inside the customer’s network.

2.caption: External
2.description: The endpoint is on the Internet or otherwise external to the customer’s network.

99.caption: Other
99.description: The network scope is not mapped. See the network_scope attribute, which contains a data source specific value.

port.caption: Port
port.description: The port used for communication within the network connection.

proxy_endpoint.caption: Proxy Endpoint
proxy_endpoint.description: The network proxy information pertaining to a specific endpoint. This can be used to describe information pertaining to network address translation (NAT).

svc_name.caption: Service Name
svc_name.description: The service name in service-to-service connections. For example, AWS VPC logs the pkt-src-aws-service and pkt-dst-aws-service fields identify the connection is coming from or going to an AWS service.
